Plot a fitted model

Source: R/plots.R
plot.fp_occu.Rd

Posterior intervals of the coefficients, or sampler diagnostics.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'fp_occu'
plot(
  x,
  type = c("intervals", "trace", "rank", "pairs"),
  pars = NULL,
  prob = 0.95,
  ...
)

Arguments

x

An fp_occu object.

type

"intervals" (default) draws the posterior median with 50% and prob intervals of every coefficient on the logit scale, one panel per process, and the standard deviations of the random effects. "trace", "rank", and "pairs" draw sampler diagnostics with 'bayesplot': trace plots and rank histograms by chain, and pairs plots with divergent transitions marked.

pars

Output names of the parameters for the diagnostics. The default takes the occupancy slopes and the parameters that are hardest to sample in this model: the false-positive intercept, the gap, and the standard deviations of the random effects.

prob

Width of the outer interval for type = "intervals".

...

Passed to the 'bayesplot' function for the diagnostics.

Value

A 'ggplot2' object (for "pairs", a 'bayesplot' grid).

See also

fp_effects(), fp_sites(), plot.fp_ppc()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
sim <- simulate_fp(nsite = 200, nocc = 10, seed = 1)
m <- fp_occu(sim$data, occ = ~ x, fp = ~ x, random_recorder = FALSE)
plot(m)
plot(m, type = "trace")
plot(m, type = "pairs", pars = c("fp_(Intercept)", "fp_gap"))
} # }
